papers.title: Coupling between molecular exchange qubits
papers.authors: Filippo Troiani, Jason S. R. McCoombs, Athanassios K. Boudalis
papers.summary: For a pair of weakly coupled molecular spin triangles, the authors derive an effective two-qubit Hamiltonian and benchmark it against the microscopic model. They predict how exchange and dipolar couplings modify electrically driven transitions between encoded states.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The transition predictions give a spectroscopic test of interactions between two molecular exchange qubits.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine arrangements of molecular spins where interactions between units determine whether individual qubits remain distinguishable.

papers.title: Long-Lived Mechanically Detected Molecular Spins for Quantum Sensing
papers.authors: Sahand Tabatabaei, Pritam Priyadarsi, Daniel Tay, Namanish Singh, Pardis Sahafi, Andrew Jordan, Raffi Budakian
papers.summary: Mechanical detection resolves an ensemble of trityl radicals in a small droplet. A modified dipolar decoupling sequence prolongs coherence sufficiently to detect alternating magnetic fields and probe nearby nuclear spins with the same molecular sensor.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: A direct experimental comparison for how molecular placement and dipolar broadening limit spin-based sensing.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine the ability to preserve electron-spin coherence in ensembles of molecular radicals.

papers.title: Emergence of Spin–Vibronic Coherence in the Intermediate Spin–Orbit Coupling Regime Revealed by Mixed Quantum-Classical Dynamics
papers.authors: Maxwell Taub, Diandong Tang, George C. Schatz, Felix N. Castellano, Lin X. Chen, Xiaosong Li
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: Simulations of five platinum dimers trace oscillations in excited-state spin populations to a resonance between platinum–platinum stretching and spin–orbit coupling. Changing the ligands moves the system into or out of this coherence regime.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The calculated resonance provides a specific vibrational mode to test when interpreting molecular spin dynamics.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate how particular molecular vibrations couple to spin degrees of freedom.

papers.title: Elusive Aluminyl Anion NHC Analogue Enables Isolation of Quasi-Linear and 2π-Aromatic Biradical B4 Fragments
papers.authors: Andreas Häfner, Maximilian Kordisch, Merle Arrowsmith, Ivo Krummenacher, Holger Braunschweig
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Reduction of a boron precursor yields two distinct four-boron motifs. Crystal structures and electronic-structure calculations support triplet biradical descriptions for both the nearly linear chain and the rearranged ring, with different roles for the surrounding aluminium fragments.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The connection to molecular qubits is synthetic: the study identifies candidate high-spin scaffolds whose spin coherence remains to be measured.

relatedPapers.reason: Both studies use molecular structure and electronic calculations to interpret stabilized radical states.

papers.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
papers.authors: Yu-Ning Zhang, Aleksandr S. Mokeev, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, David P. DiVincenzo, Viatcheslav V. Dobrovitski
papers.summary: Calculations for two-, three- and four-spin encodings compare transport trajectories under correlated noise. Moving spins in parallel generally protects coherence over short distances, while sequential motion performs better over longer distances, with the crossover set by device parameters.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Pairwise dephasing measurements give an experimental route to estimating leakage and comparing control trajectories.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine how the timing and ordering of operations affect spin coherence in the presence of noise.

papers.title: Coherent Optical Control of a Single Donor Electron Spin
papers.authors: Yuxi Jiang, Amirehsan Alizadehherfati, Christine Falter, Jasvith R. Basani, Nils von den Driesch, Yurii Kutovyi, Jan Seelbinder, Alexander Pawlis, Edo Waks
papers.summary: Optical pulses drive Rabi oscillations and Ramsey interference in a single chlorine donor electron spin in zinc selenide. Coherent population trapping also resolves signatures of hyperfine coupling to the chlorine nucleus.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The measurements give an optical protocol for distinguishing coherent electron control from electron–nuclear coupling.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate optical access to localized spins for quantum information.

papers.title: Optimal control of spin systems
papers.authors: Steffen J. Glaser, Christiane Koch, Niels Chr. Nielsen, Dominique Sugny, Dieter Suter
papers.summary: This review follows pulse design from shaped pulses and average Hamiltonian theory to numerical optimization of spin dynamics. It explains how control algorithms enable larger searches over pulse parameters across magnetic resonance and quantum technologies.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: A methodological reference for comparing pulse construction and optimization in spin-resonance experiments.

relatedPapers.reason: Both address pulse control of spins and the design of more robust operations.

papers.title: Dynamically modulated light-matter interactions for ancilla-tolerant bosonic control
papers.authors: Aniket Maiti, John W. O. Garmon, Daniel K. Weiss, Takahiro Tsunoda, Yao Lu, Steven M. Girvin, Robert J. Schoelkopf
papers.summary: Parametrically switching the coupling between a bosonic mode and its ancilla lets them idle independently. During active operations, the authors engineer coupling symmetries that limit the transfer of ancilla decay and dephasing to the oscillator.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Switchable interactions offer a control strategy for reducing errors that originate in an auxiliary degree of freedom.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate control protocols designed to limit the effects of noise during quantum operations.

papers.title: Direct-decision quantum sensing for classifying transient NMR signals
papers.authors: Juha Leppäkangas, Michael Marthaler
papers.summary: Simulated sensor-qubit controls classify transient signals from molecular spin Hamiltonians directly. Comparison with inductive readout shows that the benefit depends on signal transfer, receiver noise and available coherence time, particularly when only one sensor measurement is available.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: A close match to molecular sensing that explicitly accounts for the readout resources needed to distinguish signals.

relatedPapers.reason: Both design sensing protocols around the desired output in the presence of unwanted signal contributions.

papers.title: The Impact of Internal Electric Fields on Accurate Diamond Magnetometry
papers.authors: Jack Faller, Daphne Freda Gavras, Andrew Lowther, Romain Ruhlmann, Lilian Childress
papers.summary: A model of random internal electric fields reproduces asymmetric resonance spectra measured in nitrogen-vacancy ensembles. When the authors reconstruct known magnetic fields from simulated spectra, a modified fitting function reduces the bias of conventional fits.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: A useful calibration test for separating sensor-internal perturbations from the magnetic field being estimated.

relatedPapers.reason: Both study systematic artifacts in spin-based sensing and procedures for suppressing them.

papers.title: Competition between contrast and laser noise in laser threshold magnetometry using an external cavity diode laser
papers.authors: Shao Qi Lim, Alexander A. Wood, Brett C. Johnson, Qiang Sun, Jan Jeske, Hiroshi Abe, Takeshi Ohshima, David J. Ottaway, Heike Ebendorff-Heidepriem, Robert E. Scholten, Andrew D. Greentree, Brant C. Gibson
papers.summary: An external-cavity diode laser enhances the magnetic-resonance contrast of diamond spins near threshold. The measured field sensitivity nevertheless deteriorates because laser noise grows faster than the contrast, providing a direct test of this readout trade-off.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The experiment gives a concrete reason to measure field sensitivity alongside optical contrast when evaluating readout methods.

relatedPapers.reason: Both evaluate measurement limitations in spin-based sensors.

papers.title: Pyrrolo[3,2- b ]pyrrole Dicarboxylate Linkers Enable Topological Diversity and Tunable Luminescence in Zr6-Based Metal–Organic Frameworks
papers.authors: Liangliang Zhang, Yongkang Zeng, Yuxuan Meng, Yuheng Zeng, Xi Lin, Lixia Peng, Xiaoyuan Liu
papers.summary: Changing linker substitution and synthesis conditions produces zirconium frameworks with different network topologies and emission efficiencies. The more emissive structure also shows fluorescence quenching in response to chromium ions in water, connecting framework design to a chemical readout.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: A useful comparison of ion recognition and readout in a water-stable porous host.

relatedPapers.reason: Both demonstrate chemical sensing of ions using a functionalized framework.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage in Sensing and Imaging through Coherent Nuisance Suppression
papers.authors: Maxim Sirotin, Aleksandr Mokeev, Ishaan Kannan, Julian C. Christou, Jayadev Rajagopal, Babak Saif, Mikhail D. Lukin, Johannes Borregaard
papers.summary: The authors propose a quantum receiver that processes photon states jointly to suppress disturbances shared across samples. They derive sample savings for imaging under correlated nuisance parameters and predict the photon budget for a model of atmospheric turbulence.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: A theoretical comparison for sensing protocols where correlated background fluctuations determine the measurement cost.

relatedPapers.reason: Both exploit structured measurements to suppress unwanted contributions to a sensing signal.

papers.title: Atomically resolved exciton emission from single defects in MoS2
papers.authors: Lysander Huberich, Eve Ammerman, Yu Gu, Yining Ren, Sotirios Papadopoulos, Chengye Dong, Joshua A. Robinson, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Oliver Gröning, Lukas Novotny, Tingxin Li, Shiyong Wang, Bruno Schuler
papers.summary: The authors combine spatially resolved exciton emission with atomic-scale defect characterization in molybdenum disulfide. They assign a widespread emission band to negatively charged carbon–hydrogen complexes, connecting an optical signature to a particular defect structure.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The defect assignment offers a way to connect local spectroscopy with the electronic structure of a two-dimensional material.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine how local structure modifies electronic states in atomically thin materials.

papers.title: Pressure-Induced Luminescence Enhancement Retained after Decompression in a Gadolinium-Based Metal–Organic Framework
papers.authors: Bingqian Shi, Li-Mei Chang, Yi Zhang, Zhi-Gang Gu, Jianbo Hu, Lei Liu
papers.summary: A gadolinium framework remains more luminescent after a compression cycle and return to ambient pressure. In situ diffraction reveals an irreversible structural response. The authors propose that changes to the guest environment and retained distortion contribute to the brighter emission.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The measurements connect a processing condition to a persistent optical property in a framework solid.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate the optical response of rare-earth-containing frameworks and its dependence on the host environment.

papers.title: Unveiling the underlying spin mechanism in quasi-2D perovskite spin-polarized lasing
papers.authors: Qian Li, Zhiping Hu, Hongzhi Zhou, Zhengzheng Liu, Sihao Huang, Hao Wang, Zijun Zhan, Baihui Nie, Zeyu Zhang, Jiajun Luo, Yuxin Leng, Juan Du
papers.reviewNote: Crossref currently reports 2026-11-06, later than this issue. The feed announcement is not a verified publication date.
papers.summary: In layered perovskites, changing the organic cation modifies triplet-exciton dynamics and spin relaxation. The authors observe spin-polarized lasing below 200 K and relate the lasing threshold to the competing spin-relaxation processes.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Shows how organic constituents influence a spin-dependent optical device response in a layered material.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect chemical structure to spin dynamics and the resulting optical response.

papers.title: Local Ligand-Framework Evolution Prior to Long-Range Antiferromagnetic Ordering in NiPS3
papers.authors: Siyu Wang, Lin Ma, Danmin Liu, Guoliang Li, Yang Li, Jian Sheng, Xiaobai Ma
papers.summary: Temperature-dependent structural, magnetic and spectroscopic measurements in layered nickel phosphorus trisulfide resolve changes in the local ligand environment before neutron diffraction resolves long-range antiferromagnetic order. The onset of a magnetic response and detectable magnetic Bragg scattering occur at different temperatures.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The measurement sequence helps distinguish local structural changes from collective ordering in layered materials.

relatedPapers.reason: Both relate changes in local structure to the onset of collective phenomena in a layered solid.

papers.title: Coordination-directed synthesis of two-dimensional metal-organic covalent organic frameworks
papers.authors: Liangliang Yue, Liqin Hao, Chun Hong Mak, Binhua Chen, Duu-Jong Lee, Hsien-Yi Hsu, Jiong Zhao, Lok Wing Wong, Di Hu, Zhenjie Zhang, Xunjin Zhu
papers.summary: One-dimensional porphyrin coordination polymers provide the starting geometry for two crystalline, porous sheets formed by covalent assembly. Electron diffraction resolves the structures, and one-pot synthesis yields the same products, supporting a coordination-directed route.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The sequential and one-pot experiments provide a test for which bonding step directs framework crystallization.

relatedPapers.reason: Both investigate how the sequence of bond formation controls crystalline framework growth.

papers.title: Geometry-Induced Construction of Sub-Stoichiometric 3D Covalent Organic Frameworks for SO2 Capture
papers.authors: Jianhong Chang, Ziang Guo, Jie Zhang, Zeyue Zhang, Lin Li, Fengqian Chen, Hui Li, Valentin Valtchev, Shilun Qiu, Junliang Sun, Qianrong Fang
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Combining monomers with similar shapes but incompatible connectivities leaves regularly spaced aldehydes inside three porous frameworks. Electron and X-ray diffraction identify the partially condensed structures, and adsorption measurements show strong sulfur dioxide uptake in the functionalized pores.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Shows how incomplete condensation can be designed into a periodic lattice and verified crystallographically.

relatedPapers.reason: Both connect the chemistry of framework bond formation to the structure of crystalline products.

papers.title: Water-Cluster-Expanded Interpenetrated Covalent Organic Frameworks Create High-Affinity Coordination Microenvironments for Efficient Strontium Capture
papers.authors: Ruoqian Zhang, Tao Liu, Binhui Zheng, Anmin Lei, Shiqi Xu, Qiang Luo, Yihui Yuan, Ning Wang
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Water clusters swell an interpenetrated covalent organic framework and change how three adjacent networks coordinate strontium. Adsorption measurements and calculations link the resulting pore environment to ion selectivity and improved access to binding sites.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: The hydration-dependent binding geometry suggests a concrete variable for designing ion-recognition pockets.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use the local coordination environment of a covalent framework to recognize ions.

papers.title: pH-responsive Keto-Enol tautomerism in a β-ketoenamine covalent organic framework for selective thorium(IV) capture
papers.authors: Jiaxin Xu, Kaili Yu, Xiaofang Su, Hui Hu, Yanqiong Luo, Jiaying Qian, Muhammad Imran Anwar, Jing Zhao, Zhongliang Wen, Ming Wang, Afia Saleem, Songtao Xiao, Yanan Gao
papers.summary: A carboxyl-functionalized covalent organic framework changes its keto–enol state with pH. The altered oxygen coordination environment changes the uptake of thorium and its separation from uranium, including in strongly acidic solutions.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: Links the chemical state of the pore wall to an experimentally measured change in ion selectivity.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine framework binding pockets as determinants of chemical selectivity.

papers.title: Hexafluoroethane purification via molecular sieving in a molecule-trap metal-organic framework
papers.authors: Heng-Yu Ruan, Xin Zhang, Zhi-Wei Zhai, Jia-Mei Yu, Xuefeng Bai, Jian-Rong Li
papers.summary: Replacing oxygen with sulfur in a framework linker creates a constriction that excludes hexafluoroethane while admitting two less symmetric fluorocarbons. Breakthrough experiments on ternary mixtures test this shape-selective separation over repeated cycles.
papers.whyRelevant: Editorial assessment: A controlled linker substitution connects a small structural change to a measurable pore-selectivity change.

relatedPapers.reason: Both use ligand chemistry to program the geometry of an assembled metal–organic framework.
